Swedish Transportation Equipment Firm Appoints New Chief Executive Amid Industry Evolution

STOCKHOLM, June 12 — Swedish transportation equipment manufacturer Nordisk Mobility Group has announced the appointment of Anna Lidström as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective July 1, as the industry faces a period of rapid technological change and evolving market demands.

Lidström, 52, brings more than two decades of experience in industrial management and product development, most recently serving as Chief Operating Officer at the Gothenburg-based engineering firm ScandiaTech. She succeeds Lars Ekholm, who is retiring after leading Nordisk Mobility for eight years.

In a statement released Wednesday, Nordisk Mobility Chairman Henrik Sandberg said Lidström’s leadership would help the company “navigate an increasingly complex environment” and “capitalize on opportunities in sustainable mobility, automation, and smart infrastructure.”

“Anna’s proven track record in driving operational excellence and her keen understanding of emerging technologies make her the ideal leader for Nordisk Mobility at this pivotal moment,” Sandberg said.

Lidström said she was “honored to join a company with such a rich heritage in Swedish engineering,” adding that her immediate priorities would include “strengthening the company’s position in key export markets and advancing our electrification and digitalization strategies.”

The company, which produces railcars, heavy vehicles and urban transit solutions, is one of Sweden’s largest employers in the transport equipment sector, with more than 4,500 staff across its facilities in Västerås, Umeå and Malmö. Last year, Nordisk Mobility reported revenues of 18.6 billion kronor ($1.7 billion), with more than 60% of sales generated outside Sweden.

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment, citing Lidström’s background in both operational management and innovation. “This is a strong signal that Nordisk Mobility is looking to accelerate its transition toward greener technologies and smarter manufacturing,” said Johan Frisk, industry analyst at Skandinavisk Market Insights.

The Swedish Association of Transport Equipment Manufacturers also expressed support for the move. “As the sector adapts to new regulatory requirements and global competition, experienced leadership is crucial,” said Association chair Maria Engström. “Ms. Lidström’s expertise will be invaluable not only to Nordisk Mobility but to the wider industry.”

No organizational changes or restructuring were announced alongside Lidström’s appointment. A spokesperson for Nordisk Mobility said outgoing CEO Ekholm would remain as an advisor during a transition period through September.

The appointment comes as Sweden’s transportation equipment sector invests heavily in electrification, automation, and sustainability, supported by robust demand in Europe and Asia. The sector accounts for approximately 4.5% of Sweden’s industrial output, according to government figures.
